findings.reason: naming an external operator instead of this owner invites a second forward path beside the spine's, and the adjudication must use the operator built from the §4 geometry so its verdicts are the spine's own.
findings.text: the plan proposes Nova's Biot–Savart operators to predict loop-flux and probe-field from the mapped coil currents, but `imas_ambix/gs/operator.py` already owns exactly that: `build_operator(table)` builds a `ForwardOperator` from a `GeometryTable` (the §4 description product) and `ForwardOperator.vacuum_prediction(i_pf)` returns the PF-only sensor prediction in Wb/T, with `assemble_pf_currents` building `i_pf` from the raw coil-current channels (MMSYS on JT-60SA, amc on MAST); it is the shared owner called by `latent/data.py:457`, `statespace/enkf_baseline.py:956`, `gs/grounding.py:479`

findings.reason: §6 already chose the correct pattern for the equilibrium side ("a record contract with canonical keys… rather than writing a second scorer") and must state the same loader-boundary decision for the raw-side `ShotSignObservation`, naming the owner it extends.
findings.text: §6 says "JT-60SA supplies an observation cohort" to `cocos_convention.score_conventions` but never names the cohort builder, and the existing one, `data/cocos_convention.py:490 read_level2_observation`, is MAST-store-specific (hard-codes `MAST_LEVEL2_ROOT`, `magnetics["flux_loop_flux"]`, `equilibrium["psi"]`), so a JT-60SA cohort reader is implied as a parallel class of reader without the plan saying whether it extends `read_level2_observation`'s store seam or is a second one

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the new modules named by the plan (the §3 remote extractor + on-demand cache, the §4 deck converter, the §2 exporter) each hide substantial behaviour (ssh batch transport, deck grammar parsing, tokamap directory layout) behind one small entry point, and the §3 module already demonstrates this by reusing the zarr layout and `paths.py` owner rather than adding a reader.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §6 names "Nova's Biot–Savart operators" to predict the vacuum sensor response, but ambix already owns that forward model in `imas_ambix/gs/operator.py build_operator` / `ForwardOperator.vacuum_prediction`, fed by the same `GeometryTable` §4 produces; the owner to extend is `imas_ambix/gs/operator.py`, not an external operator.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; each surface-adding section states retirement or why nothing can be retired (§2 exporter "retires nothing, ambix has no exporter"; §3 "adds no `ambix data` command"; §4 engine extension "retires the machine branch"; §6 generalises `measure_diiid_convention` "rather than writing a second scorer"; §7 "adds two record fields and retires nothing").
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan reuses the convention scorer (`data/cocos_convention.py`) but does not cite the owner that builds the observation cohort it scores, `data/cocos_convention.py:490 read_level2_observation`, so the JT-60SA observation reader is proposed without naming what it extends.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the plan's wrappers state why the target cannot be extended: the §3 extractor declines to import imas-codex's remote layer because that would drag the graph/LLM/tool-install stack into every ambix read, and §7's EQDB reader reuses the §3 transport and cache rather than a second path.
